ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 - ENGL 442 - Contemporary British and Irish Literature - Returns of the Repressed in Contemporary British Literature - Andrew Gaedtke - This course will examine the ways that contemporary British and Irish novels are haunted by unresolved problems of the past. These problems include the global British empire and its collapse, Britain’s treatment of immigrants and postcolonial subjects, the “Troubles” in Northern Ireland, persistent gender and sexual inequality, and perennial questions about the novel’s continued relevance. Several of novels we will discuss are respond to the controversy over the UK’s departure from the European Union—a political decision that has deeply divided the nation. Using recent works of fiction as our guides, we will consider what it means to be British in the aftermath of that rupture. This course will ask how innovations in contemporary British fiction might enable us to rethink larger questions about nationality, trauma, historical reckoning, and their narration. Readings will include works by Anna Burns, Guy Gunaratne, Kazuo Ishiguro, John Lanchester, Ali Smith, and Zadie Smith.
